You are a professional biblical lexicographer fluent in Spanish. Translate the following English lexicon entry into Spanish.

Lemma: H1935

ENGLISH GLOSSES TO TRANSLATE:
  Terse gloss: "Splendor, majesty, or honor; the awe-inspiring radiance of God, royalty, or personal dignity and distinction."
  Readable gloss: "A poetic term evoking the visible, almost tangible radiance that surrounds God or a king. In worship contexts it pairs naturally with hadar ('beauty') to describe the overwhelming grandeur of the LORD (1 Chr 29:11; Ps 21:5). The multilingual evidence confirms this pairing: German renders it Majestaet and Pracht, Spanish esplendor and majestad, all clustering around royal brilliance. Yet the word can also denote a more personal dignity or honor conferred on an individual, as when Moses transfers some of his hod to Joshua (Num 27:20) or when Proverbs warns against giving away one's vigor to strangers (Prov 5:9)."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: "majesty, splendor"
    Enriched: The awe-inspiring splendor or majesty associated with God or royalty, often paired with hadar in liturgical and prophetic poetry. Translations across languages converge on 'majesty/splendor' (Ger. Majestaet, Spa. esplendor). Characteristic of divine theophany (Job 37:22) and royal enthronement (1 Chr 29:25), this sense captures the visible radiance of supreme authority.
    Existing Spanish translations: Esplendor, de-majestad-de-ti, esplendor, esplendor-de, majestad, majestad-de, majestad-suya, su-esplendor, su-majestad, tu-gloria, tu-majestad, y-esplendor-mi, y-gloria, y-la-majestad
  Sense 2: "honor, dignity"
    Enriched: Personal honor, dignity, or distinction belonging to or conferred upon an individual, emphasizing esteem and respect rather than cosmic grandeur. In Num 27:20 Moses gives some of his hod to Joshua as a transfer of authority; in Prov 5:9 it warns against squandering one's vigor or reputation. Daniel 11:21 uses it of royal dignity not rightfully bestowed.
    Existing Spanish translations: esplendor, honor-de, tu-honor
